name: registers queries and reports later matching log lines
input: two queries, two matching lines, and an unmatched line
test:
lines = ['Q: disk failed', 'L: DISK operation failed', 'Q: net error', 'L: Net error observed', 'L: unrelated text']
assert match_stream(lines) == ['ACK: disk failed; ID=1', 'M: DISK operation failed; Q=1', 'ACK: net error; ID=2', 'M: Net error observed; Q=2']

name: requires all query words while ignoring order and case
input: query words occur in a different order and case
test: assert match_stream(['Q: red BLUE', 'L: blue red', 'L: RED umbrella']) == ['ACK: red BLUE; ID=1', 'M: blue red; Q=1']

name: uses only prior queries and assigns ascending IDs
input: log before registration, then overlapping registered queries
test:
lines = ['L: go now', 'Q: red red', 'Q: go', 'L: GO now', 'Q: now', 'L: now GO RED']
assert match_stream(lines) == ['ACK: red red; ID=1', 'ACK: go; ID=2', 'M: GO now; Q=2', 'ACK: now; ID=3', 'M: now GO RED; Q=1,2,3']

name: does not match substrings and omits unmatched logs
input: fail must not match failed or failure; empty stream
test:
assert match_stream(['Q: fail', 'L: failed', 'L: failure', 'L: fail']) == ['ACK: fail; ID=1', 'M: fail; Q=1']
assert match_stream([]) == []
